steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: You may record multiple takes and submit your BEST performance — but each piece must be a single continuous take, not edited together. | Key Fact: Accompaniment can be live or backing track — the accompaniment level must not dominate your performance. Choose appropriate accompaniment for your genre. | Key Fact: Performance anxiety is normal — manage it through: thorough preparation, slow breathing, positive visualisation, and performing to others before the recording. | Key Fact: The teacher marks your performance against AQA criteria, then moderation adjusts the standard — consistency across the cohort is checked.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how performance preparation and assessment are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use performance preparation and assessment. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use performance preparation and assessment in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
